questions.question: In 1928, who discovered that when a ray of coloured light enters a liquid, a fraction of the light scattered by that liquid is of a different colour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CV Raman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman**, discovered on **28 February 1928**, that when a **beam of coloured light entered a liquid**, a fraction of the light scattered was of a different color, dependent on **material property**.
 
• This radiation effect of molecular scattering of light bears the name of ‘**Raman Effect**’, from which many applications in photonic communications and spectroscopy evolved.
 
• The Raman Effect is the process of** scattering** light particles by **molecules of a medium**.
 
• The scattering occurs due to a change in the **wavelength **of light as it enters the medium.
 
• When a **beam** of light travels through a dust-free, transparent chemical, a small fraction of the light emerges in directions other than where it should.
 
• Light consists of particles called **photons**, whose energy is directly proportional to the frequency with which they travel. 
 
• When they strike **molecules** in a medium at high speeds, they bounce back and scatter in different directions depending on the angle with which they hit the molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lord Rayleigh’s**__ first researches were mainly mathematical, concerning optics and vibrating systems, but his later work ranged over almost the whole field of physics, **covering sound, wave theory, colour vision, electrodynamics, electromagnetism, light scattering, the flow of liquids, hydrodynamics, the density of gases, viscosity, capillarity, elasticity, and photography**. 
 
• __**Satyendra Nath Bose**__ FRS was an Indian mathematician and physicist specializing in theoretical physics.
 
• He is best known for his work on **quantum mechanics** in the early 1920s, in developing the foundation for Bose statistics and the theory of the Bose condensate.
 
• **__John Tyndall__ **FRS was a prominent 19th-century Irish physicist.
 
• His initial scientific fame arose in the 1850s from his study of **diamagnetism**.

questions.question: ‘Beri-Beri’ is caused by the deficiency of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**thiamine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thiamine:**

 
 
• Thiamine, also known as Vitamin B1, is essential for energy metabolism and nerve function.
 
• A deficiency of thiamine leads to Beri-Beri.
 
• Beri-Beri can manifest in various forms, including wet Beri-Beri (affecting the cardiovascular system) and dry Beri-Beri (affecting the nervous system).
 
• Symptoms include muscle weakness, fatigue, and neurological problems.
 
• Thiamine is found in foods like whole grains, legumes, and pork.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Riboflavin:**

 
 
• Riboflavin, or Vitamin B2, is important for cell growth and energy production.
 
• A deficiency of riboflavin can cause conditions like cheilosis (cracked lips) and glossitis (inflamed tongue).
 
• It is vital for healthy skin and eyes.
 
• It is found in dairy products, eggs, and leafy green vegetables.
 
• It also helps with the metabolism of fats.
 
 
 
• **Cyanocobalamin:**
 
 
• Cyanocobalamin, or Vitamin B12, is crucial for red blood cell formation and nerve function.
 
• A deficiency of Vitamin B12 can lead to anemia and neurological problems.
 
• It is primarily found in animal products like meat, fish, and dairy.
 
• It is essential for DNA synthesis.
 
• Vegetarians and vegans may need to supplement their diet with B12.
 
 
 
• **Niacin:**
 
 
• Niacin, or Vitamin B3, is involved in energy metabolism and DNA repair.
 
• A deficiency of niacin causes Pellagra, which is characterized by dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia.
 
• It is important for healthy skin and the nervous system.
 
• Niacin is found in foods like meat, poultry, and grains.
 
• It can also be produced by the body from the amino acid tryptophan

questions.question: JJ Thomson is known for developing which model in 1898?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plum Pudding Model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• J.J. Thomson proposed the **Plum Pudding Model** of the atom in 1898 after his discovery of the electron in 1897.
 
• According to this model, the atom is composed of a positively charged sphere with negatively charged electrons embedded within it, resembling a "plum pudding."
 
• The model suggested that the positive charge is uniformly distributed throughout the atom, balancing the negative charge of the electrons.
 
• It was the first model to include the electron, an important step in understanding atomic structure.
 
• This model was later disproved by Ernest Rutherford’s Gold Foil Experiment in 1909, which led to the discovery of the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electron Discovery:**

 
 
• J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 through his experiments with cathode rays.
 
• This discovery established that atoms are divisible and contain smaller subatomic particles.
 
 
 
• **Gold Foil Experiment:**
 
 
• In 1909, Ernest Rutherford conducted the Gold Foil Experiment, which demonstrated that atoms have a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.
 
• This experiment invalidated the Plum Pudding Model, leading to the Nuclear Model of the atom.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Model Evolution:**
 
 
• The Plum Pudding Model was an early attempt to explain atomic structure but lacked experimental support for the arrangement of charges.
 
• It was followed by Rutherford’s Nuclear Model and later by Niels Bohr’s Planetary Model.
 
 
 
• **Modern Atomic Theory:**
 
 
• The current understanding of atomic structure is based on quantum mechanics, incorporating the wave-particle duality of electrons and probabilistic electron clouds.

questions.question: What is the typed, submitted or transmitted data called in a computer system?
questions.solution:
Input: Any information or data that is sent to a computer for processing is considered as input.

Output: Data generated by a computer is referred to as output. This includes data produced at a software level, such as the result of a calculation, or at a physical level, such as a printed document.

Router: A router is a networking device that forwards data packets between computer networks. Routers perform the traffic directing functions on the Internet.

Modem: A modem is a hardware device that converts data so that it can be transmitted from computer to computer over telephone wires.

questions.question: Which physicist is known to establish the relationship between mechanical work and heat transfer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Prescott Joule**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Prescott Joule** is renowned for establishing the relationship between mechanical work and heat transfer.
 
• Joule's experiments demonstrated that** heat and mechanical work are interchangeable, leading to the formulation of the first law of thermodynamics**.
 
• His work laid the foundation for** the principle of conservation of energy, **which states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted from one form to another.
 
• The unit of energy, **the joule (J), **is named in his honor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **William Henry** is known for Henry's law, which relates the solubility of gases in liquids to pressure.
 
• **Hermann Helmholtz** made significant contributions to the fields of physiology and physics, particularly in the study of energy conservation and electrodynamics.
 
• **John Dalton** is famous for his pioneering work in the development of modern atomic theory and his research on color blindness.
 
• Joule's work was pivotal in advancing the Industrial Revolution, providing a scientific basis for the efficient use of energy in engines and other machinery.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of physicists and their contributions/discoveries is INCORRECT?

options.text: Heinrich Rudolf Hertz – Generation of electromagnetic waves
Albert Einstein – Explanation of photoelectric effect
Michael Faraday – Laws of electromagnetic induction
Galileo Galilei – Wave theory of light

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galileo Galilei – Wave theory of light**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galileo Galilei** is incorrectly paired with the **wave theory of light**.
 
• Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer, physicist, and engineer, sometimes described as a polymath. He is known for his contributions to observational astronomy, including the telescopic confirmation of the phases of Venus, the discovery of the four largest satellites of Jupiter, and the observation and analysis of sunspots.
 
• The wave theory of light is primarily attributed to **Christiaan Huygens** in the 17th century and was later expanded by other scientists, including Thomas Young and Augustin-Jean Fresnel.
 
• Galileo's contributions were more focused on mechanics, motion, and astronomy rather than the wave theory of light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heinrich Rudolf Hertz** is correctly credited with the generation of electromagnetic waves. He was the first to conclusively prove the existence of electromagnetic waves by generating them in his laboratory.
 
• **Albert Einstein** is correctly known for explaining the photoelectric effect, for which he received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.
 
• **Michael Faraday** is accurately associated with the laws of electromagnetic induction, which describe how a magnetic field can interact with an electric circuit to produce an electromotive force (EMF).
 
• The correct pairing for the wave theory of light would be **Christiaan Huygens** or **Thomas Young**.

questions.question: The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) is located near ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thiruvananthapuram.**__

__
 
• The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) is located near** Thiruvananthapuram.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) was established on **21st November 1963**.
 
• The RH-75 is a rocket in the **“Rohini”** series of sounding rockets.
 
• RH-75 (Rohini-75) was the first indigenously developed rocket by ISRO (Indian Space and Research Organization) in India was launched from the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) on **20th November 1967.**
 
• Thumba is close to the **magnetic equator **and ideal for this programme.
 
• RH-75 had a **diameter of 75 mm** and hence the name. It **weighed 32 kg** and had a **height of 1.5 m**. It was a one-stage rocket. It flew 15 times between November 1967 and September 1968.
 
• In 1975, all sounding rocket activities were consolidated under one programme, the **Rohini Sounding Rocket (RSR) Programme.**
 
• The sounding rocket programme was the basis of all future launch vehicle technology that the ISRO has built. 
 
• The research in the sounding rocket domain has been led by the **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSCC) at Thiruvananthapuram.**
 
• The launch of the RH-75 was a** truly remarkable feat for a developing country**.
 
• It proved the capabilities of the Indian space scientists and researchers.
 
• The Indian space programme has truly come a long way from the small **‘toy rocket’ RH-75 to Mangalyaan, the Mars Orbiter.**
 
• **Satish Dawan Space Centre **is a rocket launch centre operated by ISRO and located in **Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: ______ is a technique in which cancer cells are damaged with radiation while limiting the harm to nearby healthy tissue.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radiotherapy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Radiotherapy to treat cancer:

 
 
• High doses of radiation are used in radiation therapy, also known as radiotherapy, as a cancer treatment to eradicate cancer cells and reduce tumour size.
 
• As with x-rays of your teeth or shattered bones, radiation is utilised at low doses in x-rays to see inside your body.
 
• Radiation therapy damages cancer cells' DNA, which either kills them or limits their growth at high dosages.
 
• Cancer cells that have DNA damage that cannot be repaired either cease proliferating or die.
 
• When the injured cells expire, the body degrades and eliminates them.
 
• But too much radiation can damage tissues by changing cell structure and damaging DNA. This can cause serious health problems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Surgery:

 
 
• Surgery is a medical speciality that employs operative manual and instrumental techniques on a patient to examine or treat a pathological condition.
 
• Such as a disease or injury, to enhance bodily function or appearance, or to repair unwelcome ruptured areas.
 
 
 
• Chemotherapy ​
 
 
• **Chemotherapy **is a drug treatment that uses powerful chemicals to kill rapidly growing cells in your body.
 
• Chemotherapy is often used to treat cancer because cancer cells grow and multiply much faster than most other cells in the body.
